pick.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +5.1%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $177.90 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-10-22, 34 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-22, 34 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-25.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-28) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.lead: What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.

stories.title: Australian wrestler Bronson Reed dies aged 38, WWE says
stories.excerpt: Tributes have flooded in for the 38-year-old Australian who is survived by his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter.
stories.lead:
Professional wrestler Bronson Reed has died aged 38, World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) has announced.

The company said the wrestler, whose real name is Jermaine Haley, died on Friday due to medical complications but did not give further details.

Paying tribute, WWE added: "Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE, but more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague."

stories.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
stories.excerpt: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, said he was remorseful for his actions.
stories.lead:
The Canadian man who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries apologised in court to the families of the victims, saying he deeply regrets his actions and will never repeat them.

Kenneth Law made the remarks on Friday during a sentencing hearing where prosecutors asked a judge to give him a 25-year prison term.

The 61-year-old pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario, Canada, though he has admitted to causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales.

stories.excerpt: Texas has been one of the most welcoming states for data centers, but that might change with a new governor coming in.
stories.lead: Under Republican Governor Greg Abbott, Texas has been one of the country's most welcoming states for new data centers. Times have changed. stories.title: Butcher blames costs for closure after 127 years
stories.excerpt: Bennett Butchers in Spalding says rises in National Insurance and energy have made it "unviable".
stories.lead:
A family butcher's shop has blamed rising costs as it prepares to close later after 127 years.

Bennett Butchers, in Spalding, Lincolnshire, was opened by Henry Bennett in 1899 and is now owned by Andrew Parsons, his great-grandson.

Parsons said the shop in Winsover Road was still popular and profitable, but a number of issues meant its future was "unviable".

stories.title: Postmortem of AI ads
stories.excerpt: The data AI companies have been accumulating in this cycle will help serve future ads to hyper-specific audiences.
stories.lead: The midterm election was a big moment for AI political advertising. Campaigns spent at least $187 million on ads, either generated or enhanced by artificial intelligence. That's according to the nonpartisan Wesleyan Media Project. These ads did not appear to affect the overall outcomes of this election, but that's not going to stop campaigns from making more of them in the next cycle. NPR political reporter Maham Javaid has more.

stories.title: Hundreds of thousands still without power a day after US slammed with Thanksgiving storms
stories.excerpt: Pennsylvania and neighbouring states remained badly affected on Friday after both coasts were lashed with wind and rain.
stories.lead:
More than 260,000 people remain without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

Eastern areas were lashed on Thursday by a powerful storm which brought high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding. Pennsylvania remained the state worst hit by power cuts early on Friday, according to monitoring site Poweroutage.us.

Conditions are now improving, though forecasters caution that it will take some time. The West Coast also was affected by its own storms.

stories.lead:
Dip, swerve, curl, whip. Hours spent mastering the craft of a great free-kick ensure those that ripple the back of the net are particularly satisfying.

This week we are digging into the Premier League's all-time best takers.

The number of goals scored from direct free-kicks has gradually decreased over the past two decades (boo!) with a rising focus on generating higher-quality chances, rather than having a pop from range.
